The insurance company has filed M.A. No.3043/2008 and the claimants have filed M.A.
No.3628/2008 against the award dated 19.09.2008 NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:25220 2 MA-3043-2008 passed in claim case No.126/2007.
The insurance company has challenged its liability inasmuch as the claims tribunal has directed for pay and recover whereas the claimants have come on the question of quantum of compensation.
2. The short facts of the case are that on 06.10.2007, the deceased Mujahid Ali was going by motorcycle of Arun Gangwal as pillion rider registration No.MP09-JQ-2298 from Indore to Mhow.

The rider of the motorcycle Arun Gangwal was riding the same in a very rash and negligent manner and when they reached near village Kailod Kartal bi-pass the deceased Mujahid Ali fell down from the motorcycle because of the rash and negligent riding of Arun Gangwal because of which he sustained grievous injuries and he was rushed to Unique Hospital, Indore where he died during Jahid Ali & Ors. vs Arun & Ors. on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34422436/
1 treatment on 13.10.2007.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Mujahid Ali.

The claims tribunal after considering the evidence on record concluded that the vehicle was being operated in breach of insurance policy, thus, the liability of payment was fastened on the owner of the vehicle.
However, a direction was given to the insurance company to first pay the amount of compensation to the claimants and then recover the same from owner.

4. The learned counsel for the insurance company submits that it was a case when at the time of filing of appeal the contention of the insurance company was that it was a case of no insurance because at the relevant time in the insurance policy the pillion rider was not treated to be covered.

Thus, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25220 3 MA-3043-2008 his contention was that it was a case of no insurance but, subsequently, Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India has clarified this position vide circular dated 16.11.2009 and in view of the same several appeals were withdrawn by the insurance company in those cases where policy was packaged policy.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As in the present case also it was a packaged policy, thus, it cannot be considered as a case of no insurance in view of the clarification of Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India.

entities.text: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 5. In this view of the matter, the appeal of the insurance company (M.A. No.3043/2008) has become infructuous and the same is hereby dismissed.

6. As regards the appeal filed by the claimants, the findings recorded by the claims tribunal in para 16 of the impugned award, the claims tribunal has taken income of the deceased at Rs.15000/- per annum on notional basis as the deceased was a student about 18 years of age at the time of his death.
7. Learned counsel for the claimants submits that the deceased was a bright student and he was preparing for IIT and considering his income as Rs.15000/- per annum is not correct and proper.
He submits that the income of the deceased should have been assessed keeping in view that he was a bright student.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurance company submits that the deceased was a student and undisputedly, he was not earning anything, thus, the claims tribunal has correctly taken his income as Rs.15000/- per annum on notional basis.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the present appeal.

9. Learned counsel for the owner contended that the liability only on the owner has been fastened for the reason that the pillion rider was not treated NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:25220 4 MA-3043-2008 as covered under the insurance policy.

However, in view of the clarification by Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India vide circular dated 16.11.2009 now without any doubt the liability is of the insurance company, hence, the owner should be relieved from liability of payment of compensation.

Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
11. From the documents exhibited as Ex.P-79 to Ex.P-82, it can be seen that the deceased had cleared class 10th and was studying in class-11th.
Considering the same, the income as assessed by the claims tribunal at Rs.15,000/- per annum appears to be on a very lower side.

In absence of any particular material for assessing the income of the deceased, the minimum wages prescribed at the relevant time for an unskilled labour are made basis for calculating the compensation.
At the relevant time, the prescribed minimum wages was Rs.2476/- per month for an unskilled labourer.

Looking to the age of the deceased as 18 years, 40% addition in his income is made and for his age,
the multiplier of 16 will apply.
Considering the fact that the deceased was bachelor, 50% deduction has to be made for his personal expenses.

12. Considering the same, the compensation for loss of dependency would come to Rs.3,32,736/-
and adding an amount of Rs.15000/- each for funeral expenses and loss of estate as well as consortium for mother and father Rs.80,000/-, the total compensation would come to Rs.4,42,736/-.

After deducting the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal Rs.2,50,598/-,
the claimants are entitled for payment of Rs.1,92,138/- in which medical NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:25220 5 MA-3043-2008 expenditure awarded by the claims tribunal Rs.70,598/-
is added, thus, the total payable amount comes to Rs.2,62,736/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the application before the claims tribunal.
13. In view of the clarification by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India, the insurance company is liable to pay entire amount of compensation.

entities.text: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly, the appeal of the claimants (M.A. No.3628/2008) stands allowed on above terms and the appeal of insurance company (M.A. No.3043/2008) is dismissed.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
